text: Oh -- hello! Sorry, I didn't hear the door. Are you new? You look new. I don't mean that badly.
I'm Wren. I'm twenty kyu, which sounds impressive until you learn that twenty kyu is the bottom of the ladder and I'm holding it up.
There's a beginner tournament in six weeks. The Cup. Marguerite runs it and she is terrifying about pairings.
Everyone here is getting ready for it. That's why the tables are all out.
If you're going to enter you should get a rank first, and for that you need to actually play somebody.
That's Kesh over there, by the window. Twelve kyu. She'll play anyone, immediately, and she remembers every result.
She's not mean about it. She's just... keeping a list.
Do you want me to explain how a game ends? People find that bit odd at first.
When neither of you can find a move worth playing, you both pass. That's it. Nobody dies, nobody wins on time.
Then you count: your surrounded empty points, plus any stones you captured. Highest total wins.
White gets a few extra points for going second. Komi. It's five and a half on a small board, so there are no draws.
Good. That's the right attitude and I don't have it.
Go on. She's already looking at you.
Kesh is by the window. She's been waiting since you walked in, she just won't say so.
You BEAT her? On your first game here?
I have played Kesh eleven times. Would you like to guess my record. Go on, guess it.
Sorry. I'm genuinely pleased. She'll want a rematch within the hour, you understand that.
Ah. Yes. She does that.
For what it's worth you had a real position in the bottom left and then you tried to save everything at once.
That's the whole of my Go knowledge, by the way. You can have it.
Have you played before? Be honest, nobody here minds either way.

choices.text: Never. I don't know the rules at all.
I know how the stones move.
A bit. Remind me of the capturing rule.

text: There. That is the whole rulebook, near enough -- liberties, capture, and no filling in your own last one.
Everything else people say about Go is a consequence of those three things, said at greater length.
Oh -- before you go. I told you that was the whole rulebook and it was very slightly a lie.
There is one more rule and I left it out because it is the strange one and I did not want to frighten you off. Can I show you now?
That's fair. It's not one you need until it happens to you, and then you'll want it badly.
